title: Hello all, I just wanted to share my game with people who might enjoy it, since I am having fun playing.
author: Reasonable_Key_965
selftext:
This is my first post. Hope I got everything right.

…

The Game: TetraNinja

[https://tetraninja.itch.io/play](https://tetraninja.itch.io/play)

I don't know how to describe TetraNinja's genre because I am not sure what actually fits it correctly. It kinda is:

\- incremental

\- procedurally generated (with seed system)

\- roguelite (very lite) through permanent skill increases and permadeath

\- 3D platformer survival

…

Inspiration:

With passion for old-school arcade games and modern roguelites, I wanted to experience how the controls of the classic game "N" could feel in a 3D environment.

There is also heavy influence from Mario 64's movement/controls, because the floaty feel of N does not work with the steadily faster-falling Tetracubes.

NBALL by Ragdollsoft was also an inspiration (shoutout to those old-school indie devs and anyone who actually knows what I am talking about).

…

How it came to be and what the intention is:



AI, but is it SLOP? You decide.

I vibecoded TetraNinja over a period of 14 months with only free-tier LLM subscriptions as a side project, with Little to no background in coding. It started around August 2025 in a simple chat with Gemini. I wanted to create a 2.5D Tetris game where you could control a little ninja, interact with the tetrominos, and "nag" the AI playing the actual game. It was not very fun. So I thought: how hard could it be to make it 3D since we were already almost there…

Man, was I wrong.

For this, I then moved the project to Google Firebase Studio at some point in September. We created the general structure as a proof of concept there. The AI and I were pretty burned out around late 2025, so I took a break and worked on it only occasionally. I heard about OpenCode and the Big Pickle model early in 2026, and with agentic coding I was able to continue working on the project, since it had already gotten pretty large and hard to maintain. This is what I am still using.

We made multiple refactors, improved/hardened systems and implementations, fused logic, and added a lot of optimizations to make TetraNinja actually run pretty smoothly for all that's going on (Web Workers, frustum culling, instanced meshing, optimizing shaders, and a lot more).

It is now almost finished for what it is supposed to be. The game is perfectly playable, and I have not encountered any game-breaking bugs during playthroughs. I am currently still working on some minor glitches and animations, and the friction/velocity system will get a complete overhaul when I am satisfied with it. Maybe some more elemental blocks will be added in the future.

  
Also, there currently is **only controller support, no mobile controls!** The reason is that I still have no idea how moving both sticks and pressing a button at the same time can work with mobile controls.

Sounds were created with ElevenLabs, and models and rigging with 3D model-generating tools. I vibecoded a tool to animate the model myself, since no free animations were even close to the ninja's actions in-game. This is why some animations look kinda wonky for now.

…

Yeah, I think this covers it.  
Feedback is very appreciated.

Thank you for providing the opportunity to share what has become a part of my life.
